QF.id: AIFM CII Fund Performance and Benchmarking_29

question.text: Priya's Growth Fund XYZ (Cat I AIF) has Net IRR of 12.77%, portfolio beta of 1.3, risk-free (repo) rate of 5.60%, and 1-year CRISIL AIF Index Cat I return of 9.25%. Using CAPM, Alpha (α) of the fund is:

explanation.text: **The Logic:** CAPM Expected Return E(R) = Rf + β × (Rm - Rf) = 5.60% + 1.3 × (9.25% - 5.60%) = 5.60% + 1.3 × 3.65% = 5.60% + 4.745% = 10.345%. Alpha = Net IRR - E(R) = 12.77% - 10.35% = 2.42%. Matches PDF Example 7.5 best-case. **The Trap:** 3.52% uses beta of 1.0. 7.17% forgets to subtract Rf inside bracket. -1.60% is nonsensical. **Cross-Exam Context:** XIX-C uses identical CAPM alpha. XXI-B, XV also rely on CAPM for alpha computation of listed portfolios. **Manager's Pro-Tip:** Chapter 7 itself flags CAPM limitations for Cat I/II — beta of unlisted book is estimated, not observed. Caveat any CAPM-alpha number in LP reports with 'beta estimated using listed-proxy regression'.
